Alternative methods, such as microincisions, diamond drills, and diathermy, yielded mixed results and often required multiple sessions. Long-term outcome data were scarce.

CONCLUSION: Best practice appears to combine prompt removal of foreign material in the acute phase with appropriate laser therapy for established traumatic tattoos. The overall evidence is low-level and heterogeneous, and prospective comparative studies with longer follow-up are required.

articles.title: Patterns of depression screening, referral, and behavioral health follow-up after orthopaedic trauma.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate baseline patterns of depression, behavioral health referral, and behavioral health treatment among orthopaedic trauma patients at a Level I trauma center.

METHODS: Design: Retrospective Cohort, Secondary Analysis Setting: Single Level 1 Trauma Center Patient selection criteria: Adult orthopaedic trauma patients who completed an ambulatory postoperative visit between September 2024 and November 2025. Outcome measures and comparisons: Demographic variables, PHQ-9 screening results, injury characteristics, behavioral health referral patterns, and referral completion were extracted from institutional electronic health records. Primary outcomes were the proportion of patients screening positive for depression (PHQ-9 >10), with moderately severe to severe depression (PHQ-9 ≥15) triggering behavioral health referral, and subsequent referral completion rates. Secondary outcomes included referral patterns by injury mechanism and six-month orthopaedic complications or unplanned healthcare utilization.

RESULTS: Among 528 patients, 44.7% (236/528) screened positive for depressive symptoms, and 21.2% (112/528) demonstrated moderately severe to severe depression triggering a behavioral health referral. 33.9% (38/112) of referred patients completed a behavioral health visit compared with 67.6% (115/170) of referred non-trauma orthopaedic patients. The severe depression cohort was on average younger and more likely to be female, black, and have Medicare/Medicaid insurance status. Injury Severity Score did not differ significantly across depression categories. Patients with ballistic injury had significantly higher rates of positive depression screening (51.9% vs. 41.8%; P = 0.040) and behavioral health referrals (34.0% vs. 18.0%; P < 0.001) than non-ballistic patients, though referral completion did not differ significantly by mechanism (25.0% ballistic vs. 38.2% non-ballistic; P = 0.198). Infectious and wound complications and unplanned healthcare utilization, driven by emergency department visits for wound complications, were significantly higher among patients who screened positive and failed to complete their referral compared with those who screened negative for depression (P < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Significant gaps exist in the depression care cascade for orthopaedic trauma patients. Referral completion rates were approximately two-fold lower than non-trauma orthopaedic subspecialties, and referral non-completion was associated with significantly higher rates of infectious complications and unplanned healthcare utilization. Targeted, navigation-based interventions addressing structural barriers at the point of care are needed to close the gap between depression identification and treatment engagement in orthopaedic trauma.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III.

articles.title: Predictors of 30-day mortality and complications following surgical treatment of pathologic hip fractures.
articles.abstract: Pathologic hip fractures present complex challenges and are associated with higher postoperative complication rates and mortality compared with non-pathologic fractures. This study aimed to compare 30-day outcomes between pathologic and non-pathologic hip fracture patients and identify factors associated with 30-day mortality and postoperative complications among patients with pathologic hip fractures using the National Surgical Quality Improvement Program database. A retrospective analysis was conducted from 2006 to 2023. Patients aged ≥ 18 years undergoing hip fracture surgery were included. Patients with non-pathologic hip fractures were compared with those with pathologic hip fractures. Univariate analyses and multivariable logistic regression models were used to identify factors associated with pathologic hip fracture 30-day mortality and complications. Among 204,675 hip fracture patients, 6159 (2.9%) had pathologic hip fractures. Patients with pathologic hip fractures had higher rates of 30-day mortality (7.8% vs. 5.1%, p < 0.001), any postoperative complication (35.3% vs. 30.2%, p < 0.001), cardiac/transfusion complications (27.5% vs. 22.2%, p < 0.001), renal complications (0.5% vs. 0.3%, p = 0.017), and venous thromboembolic complications (3.4% vs. 1.7%, p < 0.001). Infectious complications and neurological complications were not significantly different between groups. In multivariable analyses, prominent protective factors associated with decreased 30-day mortality included absence of disseminated cancer (aOR 0.4, p < 0.001), independent functional status (aOR 0.2, p < 0.001), and absence of sepsis history (aOR 0.4, p = 0.02). Thrombocytopenia (aOR 1.9, p < 0.001) and anemia (aOR 1.9, p < 0.001) were prominent risk factors for 30-day mortality. Thrombocytopenia and anemia were also significant risk factors for any complications and cardiac/transfusion complications. These findings underscore the importance of comprehensive preoperative assessment and multidisciplinary care to optimize outcomes for patients with pathologic hip fractures. Patients with multiple risk factors for adverse postoperative morbidity and mortality should receive appropriately tailored care.

articles.title: Video-assisted resident education is associated with improved ankle joint reduction: A prospective controlled study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Proper fracture reduction and splinting technique is critical for soft tissue protection and fracture stability in the acute management of ankle fractures. However, residency education for acute ankle fracture reduction and splinting techniques remains poorly standardized and streamlined. This study evaluated the effect of implementing a video-assisted ankle fracture management education program administered to first-year orthopaedic residents on ankle joint reduction and splint quality.

METHODS: This was a prospective controlled study conducted at a single level I trauma center. All consecutive ankle fractures (OTA/AO: 4F, 44) requiring the placement of a bivalved short leg cast or AO splint from January 1, 2019, to June 30th, 2022 were included. Exclusion criteria included skeletal immaturity, missing imaging, delayed fracture presentation more than two weeks from injury, concurrent ipsilateral injury/polytrauma interfering with ankle reduction, open fracture, or ankle fractures treated without an AO splint or cast. The primary outcome was joint reduction quality defined as radiographic post-reduction tibiofibular overlap, tibiofibular clear space, and medial clear space. Secondary outcomes included splint padding thickness and ankle dorsiflexion angle to assess splint quality.

RESULTS: A total of 280 consecutive ankle fracture cases were included for evaluation of splint quality: 111 in the intervention group (mean age 46; [range 14-92]; 44% female) versus 169 in the control group (mean age 44; [range 14-90]; 41% female). Comparable injury severity was observed between groups. In the supination-external rotation IV (SER4) and type IV-equivalent (SER4e) subgroup, there was significant improvement in joint reduction quality in the intervention group as compared to control (55% versus 36%, respectively; Risk Ratio: 1.52, [95% CI: 1.03-2.25], p = 0.04). In the entire cohort, splint padding thickness was not significantly improved in the intervention group (p > 0.05), however, there was a significant increase in the percentage of ankles splinted in an appropriately dorsiflexed position (p = 0.03).

CONCLUSIONS: Implementation of video-assisted ankle fracture management education program was associated with improvements in overall ankle joint reduction quality. While the clinical significance of the improvements observed in ankle reduction remains yet to be established, orthopaedic surgery residency programs should consider incorporating video technique guides into their educational curricula.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level II, Therapeutic Study.

articles.title: Opportunistic assessment of bone quality using CT-derived hounsfield units in postmenopausal women with femoral trochanteric fractures.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: CT-derived Hounsfield unit (HU) measurements may provide an opportunistic assessment of bone density when dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) is difficult to obtain during acute treatment of femoral trochanteric fractures. We compared three femoral-head regions of interest (ROIs) and explored their ability to identify markedly low total hip bone mineral density (BMD).

METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 87 women aged ≥ 65 years with AO/OTA type 31A1 (excluding A1.1) or 31A2 femoral trochanteric fractures treated with intramedullary nailing. Admission CT HU values were measured in three femoral-head ROIs on coronal and axial images and compared with contralateral hip DXA T-scores measured approximately 1 week after surgery. Pearson correlations and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses were performed. The prespecified total hip T-score thresholds were ≤ -2.5 and ≤ -3.3; the latter was used as an operational definition of markedly low BMD in this study.

RESULTS: Coronal whole-femoral-head HU values (ROI 1) showed a moderate correlation with total hip T-scores (r = 0.569). For the ≤ -2.5 threshold, 74 women met the criterion and only 13 did not; the ROI 1 coronal AUC was 0.841. For the ≤ -3.3 threshold, 51 women met the criterion and 36 did not. A coronal ROI 1 threshold of < 158.7 HU had an AUC of 0.765 (95% CI, 0.660-0.870), sensitivity of 84.3% (43/51), and specificity of 66.7% (24/36) for identifying a total hip T-score ≤ -3.3.

CONCLUSION: Whole-femoral-head HU values were moderately associated with DXA-derived T-scores in this cohort. Admission CT may help flag patients with markedly low BMD, but the threshold showed limited specificity and requires external validation. Its effect on surgical decisions or clinical outcomes was not assessed.

articles.title: Thoracic irrigation in managing traumatic hemothorax: A concise review of techniques and practice variations.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Retained hemothorax following tube thoracostomy occurs in up to one-third of thoracic trauma patients, often necessitating additional interventions. Thoracic irrigation has emerged as a potential adjunct to improve pleural drainage. The objective of this concise review is to evaluate the role of thoracic irrigation in the management of traumatic hemothorax by highlighting current standards of care and variations in techniques.

METHODS: This review searched five search engines, screening studies published before September 26, 2025. Studies focusing on thoracic irrigation in the setting of trauma and hemothorax were included.

RESULTS: A total of six studies were included. Thoracic irrigation in the management of traumatic hemothorax showed significantly lower odds of secondary intervention (OR: 0.16, p < 0.001) and shorter hospital length of stay (7 days vs. 9, p = 0.04) in patients who received thoracic irrigation compared with standard chest tube drainage. Most patients underwent irrigation using medium to large-bore tubes, although one study showed no association between tube size and outcomes. Patients receiving ≥ 1000 milliliters (mL) of irrigation had more hospital-free days compared to those receiving < 1000 mL (p = 0.007), while another study found no significant differences.

CONCLUSION: Thoracic irrigation shows promise as an adjunct to tube thoracostomy in managing post-traumatic hemothorax, with evidence of reduced retained collections, fewer secondary interventions, and shorter hospital stays. Studies are needed to achieve standardized thoracic irrigation techniques and develop more comprehensive and consistent evidence-based guidelines.

articles.title: Do radiographic surrogates of pre-bend appropriateness influence outcomes after titanium elastic nailing in pediatric femoral mid-shaft fractures?
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate whether radiographic technical parameters reflecting pre-bend appropriateness are associated with radiographic and clinical outcomes after titanium elastic nailing (TEN) in pediatric femoral mid-shaft fractures.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 85 children aged 5-11 years treated with TEN between 2015 and 2025. Constructs were classified as criteria-met (n = 38) or criteria-unmet (n = 47) using nail symmetry, a bend apex-fracture apex distance ratio ≤ 10%, and a metaphyseal spread ratio ≥ 50%. Separate exploratory multivariable models evaluated the composite classification and its components, adjusting for clinical and technical covariates.

RESULTS: Median coronal angulation was lower in the criteria-met group (2.0° vs 5.0°; p = 0.005). The adjusted mean difference (criteria-unmet minus criteria-met) was 3.42° (95% CI 0.98-5.87; p = 0.007). Other group comparisons were inconclusive. Exploratory component analysis associated greater spread with greater limb length discrepancy (3.61 mm per increase of 10 %age points; 95% CI 1.81-5.40; q = 0.002), although technical parameters were highly correlated. The complication risk ratio for criteria-unmet versus criteria-met constructs was 1.41 (95% CI 0.45-4.48).

CONCLUSION: Meeting the study-specific radiographic criteria was associated with lower coronal angulation, but its clinical importance remains uncertain. Overlapping criteria, correlated technical parameters, and limited precision preclude conclusions of equivalence or definitive independent effects.

articles.title: Scapular fracture and risk of great vessel injury in geriatric blunt trauma: A TQIP analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Scapular fractures are markers of high-energy blunt thoracic trauma and may indicate severe intrathoracic injury. Despite the substantial mortality linked with great vessel injuries (GVI), data specifically examining scapular fracture and GVI in the geriatric population remain limited. We hypothesized that scapular fracture, particularly when accompanied by concomitant thoracic fractures, is independently associated with GVI in geriatrics with blunt trauma.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the American College of Surgeons Trauma Quality Improvement Program (ACS-TQIP) database (2017-2023). Patients aged ≥ 65 years with a blunt mechanism of injury and AIS severity 2-5 in the neck, thorax, or upper extremity were included. GVI was defined using specific AIS codes for major thoracic and cervical vessels. Multivariable logistic regression evaluated association between scapular fracture patterns and GVI, including isolated scapular fractures, those with concomitant sternal, rib or flail chest fractures. Models adjusted for age, sex, race, mechanism, ISS, shock index, and modified frailty index. Vessel-specific analyses were also performed. Primary outcome was GVI. Secondary outcomes were mortality and LOS.

RESULTS: A total of 677,134 patients were included. Median age was 76 [70-82] years; 54.1% were female. Scapular fractures were identified in 5.0% of patients and GVI in 0.7%. In multivariable regression, isolated scapular fracture was associated with lower odds of GVI (aOR 0.783, 95% CI 0.704-0.871, p < 0.001), while scapular fracture with sternal fracture was associated with significantly higher odds (aOR 1.423, 95% CI 1.122-1.806, p = 0.004). Among vessel-specific analyses, subclavian artery injury demonstrated the highest association with scapular fracture (aOR 1.527, 95% CI 1.113-2.094, p = 0.009). GVI was associated with markedly higher in-hospital mortality (25.1% vs. 4.2%; OR 7.726, 95% CI 7.234-8.251, p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: In geriatric blunt trauma, isolated scapular fracture is not an independent predictor of GVI. After a fall, a scapular fracture without a sternal fracture does not by itself suggest a missed vascular injury. In contrast, combined scapular and sternal fractures represent a high-risk pattern that warrants a heightened index of suspicion and a low threshold for CT angiography, with particular attention to the subclavian vessels.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Prognostic/Epidemiologic; Level III.

articles.title: Orthopedic trauma in patients with opioid use disorder: Current concepts in perioperative management.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Opioid use disorder (OUD) is an important challenge in orthopedic trauma, where acute injury intersects with preexisting opioid exposure, tolerance, complex pain, and barriers to continuity of addiction treatment. OUD has been associated with higher rates of complications, readmission, and treatment disruption, yet OUD-specific perioperative management remains inconsistently incorporated into orthopedic trauma practice. This review synthesizes the epidemiology, outcomes, and perioperative management evidence for this population.

METHODS: A clinically oriented current concepts review synthesized peer-reviewed literature, prioritizing studies published from 2013 onward. PubMed and Embase were searched, supplemented by Google Scholar, Semantic Scholar, and manual review of reference lists from relevant articles. Studies examining perioperative outcomes, multimodal analgesia, and management of medications for OUD (MOUD) relevant to orthopedic trauma were included; studies limited to pediatric, elderly, or prenatal populations were excluded.

RESULTS: Preinjury opioid exposure is common among orthopedic trauma patients, whereas formally diagnosed OUD is less prevalent, affecting approximately 1% of operative trauma patients and up to 2.3% of patients with open lower-extremity fractures. OUD and opioid-related disorders are associated with higher rates of infection, nonunion, revision, prolonged hospitalization, and readmission. Consensus guidance and observational evidence support continuation of evidence-based MOUD, individualized opioid supplementation, multimodal nonopioid analgesia, regional anesthesia when appropriate, and early coordination with addiction and acute pain services. Guideline-based approaches to postoperative opioid prescribing, tapering, and patient education are also summarized.

CONCLUSIONS: Orthopedic trauma patients with OUD require individualized, multidisciplinary perioperative care. The strongest available evidence supports preservation of OUD treatment, multimodal analgesia, early addiction and pain consultation, and coordinated discharge planning rather than either opioid avoidance or opioid-only treatment. The review concludes with the authors' recommendations for the operating surgeon, including in-hospital and outpatient tapering plans, management of requests for additional opioids, and patient education.

articles.title: The downside of the pull-up: A 10-year national analysis of emergency department visits, 2015-2024.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To characterize the epidemiology and clinical patterns of injuries related to pull-up and chin-up bars in a nationally representative emergency department (ED) dataset.

METHODS: Retrospective cross-sectional analysis of the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission National Electronic Injury Surveillance System from January 1, 2015, to December 31, 2024. Cases were identified using product code 3277 with narrative filters for "pull-up," "chin-up," and "doorway bar," excluding barbells and playground equipment. NEISS sampling weights produced national estimates. Annual totals with 95 % confidence intervals were calculated and reported. Injury characteristics were summarized by age group, body region, diagnosis, location, disposition, and a narrative-derived mechanism category (fall, struck by bar, slip or detachment, other).

RESULTS: An estimated 40,987 ED visits were attributed to pull-up bar injuries, averaging about 4000 per year, with a peak in 2024 (5421; 95 % CI, 5315-5527). Patients were predominantly male (66.1 %) with a bimodal age distribution centered on children 5-14 years and adults 18-34 years. Craniofacial trauma predominated, with head and face together comprising nearly one-half of presentations, followed by upper-extremity involvement, including shoulder, wrist, and forearm. Laceration, internal head injury, and fracture were the leading diagnoses, with sprain or strain and contusion also frequent. Most incidents occurred in the home, and 93.8 % of patients were treated and released. Falls were the most common mechanism, followed by struck-by events and a subset explicitly involving bar slip or detachment.

CONCLUSIONS: Pull-up bar injuries constitute a consistent national burden of craniofacial and upper-extremity trauma concentrated in youth and young adults, largely managed nonoperatively in acute care settings. Improved recognition of exercise-associated injury mechanisms may assist diagnostic accuracy and reduce the burden on emergency and orthopedic services.

articles.title: How the cause of surgical delay affects mortality in fragility hip fractures: A cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prompt surgery for fragility hip fractures is a cornerstone of care and a key metric within the Best Practice Tariff (BPT) in the United Kingdom. Yet, since 2011, time to theatre has steadily increased, BPT adherence has fallen, and paradoxically, mortality has reduced. It is still unclear if surgical delay is an independent predictor of mortality. Emerging evidence suggests that the causes of surgical delays may be more important determinants of mortality than the delay itself.

METHODS: A cohort study of 1769 hip fracture patients above the age of 60 was conducted in a single centre in England. This study collected demographic data, timing to theatre (<36 h vs ≥36 h), reasons for any delays, 30-day mortality and 1-year mortality between March 2020 and December 2024.

RESULTS: The most common cause of delay was insufficient theatre capacity (N = 365, 20.6%), followed by delays awaiting medical stabilisation (N = 102, 5.8%). Age (Χ2 71.638 p < 0.001), ASA grade (Χ2 37.045 p < 0.001), sex (Χ2 27.721 p < 0.001), pre-admission residence (Χ2 36.772 p < 0.001), and reason for delay (Χ2 27.495 p = 0.007) were significant predictors of mortality. Delays due solely because of theatre unavailability did not increase 30-day (OR 0.784 p = 0.398) or 1-year mortality (OR 1.123 p = 0.474). In contrast, delays due to medical optimisation were associated with markedly higher 30-day (OR 3.573, p < 0.001) and 1-year mortality (OR 2.144, p = 0.005).

CONCLUSIONS: While early surgery remains beneficial, patients delayed solely due to administrative reasons did not demonstrate an associated increase in mortality. Mortality associated with operative delay was primarily associated amongst patients with concurrent acute illnesses and co-morbidities, independently increasing risk. To improve mortality, the focus must remain on pre-operative optimisation and robust orthogeriatric assessment, rather than surgical timing alone. Future iterations of the BPT may benefit from incorporating the cause of delay and physiological risk stratification to surgical timing targets to better align national incentives with clinical outcomes.

articles.title: The blunt truth: The role of marijuana in PTSD after intentional traumatic injury.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Survivors of interpersonal violence experience high rates of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), and rates of marijuana use are rising among young adults. There is however, limited understanding of marijuana use patterns among survivors of interpersonal violence with PTSD. We evaluated relationships between PTSD and marijuana use following injury and hypothesized that PTSD-positive patients would report elevated follow-up marijuana use.

METHODS: Between 10/2019 and 7/1/2024, we prospectively collected data on patient demographics, PTSD, substance use (including marijuana), and PROMIS-29 quality of life domains for adult trauma patients admitted to an urban, academic, level-1 trauma center. Participants were screened at baseline and at 6- or 12-month follow-up. Injury characteristics were collected from the institutional trauma registry. Among the intentionally injured, we compared patients by follow-up PTSD screening results. We excluded patients who screened positive for PTSD at baseline. Using multivariable logistic regression we assessed relationships between follow-up PTSD and marijuana use, including demographic and injury characteristics as covariates. Our primary outcome was dichotomized follow-up marijuana use.

RESULTS: Of 105 participants injured by intentional trauma with complete follow-up data, 69 screened negative for PTSD at baseline and therefore were included in this analysis. Patients who screened positive for PTSD at follow-up had greater marijuana use at baseline (29% vs 3%, p = 0.002) and follow-up (42% vs 13%, p = 0.007), and worse PROMIS-29 scores in all domains (p ≤ 0.01), compared to PTSD-negative patients. In multivariable analysis, screening positive for PTSD was associated with 7.1 times greater odds of marijuana use at follow-up (p = 0.007, CI:1.7, 29.5).

CONCLUSIONS: PTSD and marijuana use were closely associated in survivors of interpersonal violence. Screening efforts should account for marijuana use specifically. Routine screening for marijuana use could improve recognition of psychological challenges after trauma and could help identify patients at risk for development of PTSD.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III, prognostic/epidemiological.

articles.title: Pediatric flexor tendon injuries: A 13-year retrospective review of injury characteristics, treatment, and outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric flexor tendon injuries are rare but potentially devastating. Due to low incidence, optimal perioperative management remains poorly defined, and evidence is scarce. This study evaluates the injury characteristics, surgical treatment, age-specific functional outcomes, and challenges in this population.

METHODS: A retrospective review was conducted on 79 pediatric patients (mean age 6.84 ± 4.27 years; 67.1% male) who underwent surgical repair for flexor tendon lacerations between 2010 and 2023. Outcomes were assessed using Total Active Motion (TAM), Strickland score, grip/pinch strength, Semmes-Weinstein monofilament, two-point discrimination, and QuickDASH questionnaire, with a mean follow-up of 59.9 ± 32.8 months.

RESULTS: Zone 2 was the most common injury site (45.6%), with glass being the predominant mechanism (67.1%). Nerve injury was present in 35.4% of cases. Overall, good/excellent results were achieved in 81.9% (TAM) and 89.0% (Strickland) of patients. The 0-5 years age group had significantly lower Strickland scores than the 6-12 years group (74.28% vs. 82.9%, p < 0.05). Zone 5 injuries demonstrated significantly better outcomes than Zone 2 and 3 (p < 0.001). The overall complication rate was low (5.1%), with a rerupture rate of 2.5%.

CONCLUSION: Pediatric flexor tendon repairs yield favorable functional outcomes with low complication rates. Age-related differences in functional outcomes should be interpreted cautiously because of developmental differences in patient cooperation and age-dependent rehabilitation strategies. Concomitant nerve injury was associated with poorer functional outcomes. The modified Kessler technique remains a reliable repair method.

articles.title: Quantitative decision-support strategies to enhance emergency medical service accessibility in high-risk freeway tunnels.
articles.abstract: Crashes inside road tunnels often result in more severe outcomes due to spatial constraints that delay prehospital emergency medical services (EMS) access. Emergency evacuation facilities, such as cross passages and emergency parking areas, are critical for ensuring timely EMS response during traffic congestion caused by in-tunnel crashes. This study presents a quantitative approach to develop targeted strategies for enhancing such facilities to improve EMS accessibility in tunnels. Nationwide in-tunnel crash data from Korean freeways over a four-year period were analyzed, and the limited number of severe crash cases was addressed using SMOTE-based data augmentation to balance severity levels in the prediction model. A SHAP-based XGBoost classifier was applied to identify the influence of key features related to EMS accessibility and emergency evacuation facilities on crash severity. The results showed that crashes occurring more than 1 km from the tunnel entrance and EMS response coverage within a 10-15 km range have a significant impact on increasing crash severity. The presence of emergency cross passages, three or more lanes, emergency parking areas, and properly spaced CCTV installations were found to help reduce crash severity. Based on these findings, tunnels with particularly limited EMS accessibility were prioritized, and tailored facility improvement measures were proposed. This study provides quantitative evidence to guide cost-effective upgrades of tunnel emergency evacuation facilities, enhancing prehospital EMS accessibility and emergency preparedness. The proposed methodology can also support decision-making on implementing road tunnel safety improvement policies.

articles.title: Acellular fish-skin grafting complex soft tissue defects in orthopedic trauma: Technique and outcomes of a consecutive case series.
articles.abstract: This article describes a surgical technique for applying an acellular fish-skin graft (Kerecis Omega3 Wound; Kerecis, Ísafjörður, Iceland) in orthopedic trauma and reports outcomes from a consecutive series of patients treated at an urban Level I trauma center. After institutional review board approval, we reviewed 27 adult patients with complex extremity wounds who were treated with acellular fish-skin grafting between January 1st, 2023, and December 30th, 2025. Wound etiologies included traumatic soft tissue injuries, postoperative wound dehiscence, necrotizing soft tissue infections, and chronic osteomyelitis with associated soft tissue compromise. Acellular fish-skin grafting was indicated in this series of patients for full-thickness skin loss (or deeper), including those with exposed tendons, bone, or ligaments, in whom flap reconstruction was contraindicated. Patients underwent serial irrigation and debridement followed by application of an acellular fish-skin graft. The primary outcome was complete wound healing without flap-based soft-tissue reconstruction. Secondary outcomes included the number of graft applications, duration of negative-pressure wound therapy (NPWT), time to split-thickness skin grafting (STSG), and all complications. Acellular fish-skin grafting facilitated wound healing in most patients, including those with infection, exposed bone, tendon, and/or ligaments, and substantial medical and social comorbidities. Twenty-two patients (84%) achieved definitive wound coverage without flap reconstruction. Five patients (19%) were referred to plastic surgery after grafting. Two ultimately achieved limb salvage with local wound care alone, whereas the remaining three required amputation. None of the referred patients were salvaged with flap reconstruction. One patient died on postoperative day two from unrelated medical causes, and one was lost to follow-up. Consequently, acellular fish-skin grafting may be a useful adjunct in managing complex orthopedic trauma wounds, particularly in high-risk patients or in settings with limited access to reconstructive surgery. Prospective comparative studies are needed to better define indications, effectiveness, and cost-effectiveness.

articles.title: Peripheral nerve blocks reduce opioid requirements in the first 24 h following surgical fixation of acute tibial shaft fractures.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the effect of peripheral nerve blocks (PNB) on postoperative opioid use, length of stay (LOS), and incidence of acute compartment syndrome (ACS) in patients presenting with acute tibial shaft fractures treated with intramedullary nail (IMN) fixation.

METHODS: Design: Retrospective cohort study Setting: Level 1 Academic Trauma Center from 2018 to 2022. Patient Selection Criteria: Patients aged 18-79 years with acute AO/OTA 42A-C tibial shaft fractures treated with IMN within 7 days of injury Outcome Measures and Comparisons: The primary outcome was postoperative opioid use, measured in morphine milligram equivalents (MME), during hospital stay, up to a maximum of 72 h after surgery. Patients who received a preoperative PNB were compared to those who did not receive a block. Secondary outcomes included postoperative LOS and incidence of ACS.

RESULTS: 246 patients were eligible for analysis of which 78 (32%) received a PNB (PNB=yes) and 168 (68%) did not (PNB=no). Mean MME were significantly lower in the PNB=yes group compared to the PNB=no group at 24 h (73 vs. 138, p < 0.001). Controlling for age, Injury Severity Score (ISS), and time to surgery, a multivariable regression model demonstrated a 36% reduction in MME per hour for patients that received PNBs. There were 3 cases of ACS in PNB=No and 1 in PNB=Yes. All 3 patients without a PNB were diagnosed within 2 days of surgery and underwent uncomplicated fasciotomies. One patient with a PNB re-presented to the hospital 5 days postoperatively, underwent fasciotomies, and was found to have anterior and lateral compartment necrosis.

CONCLUSION: PNBs for select acute tibial shaft fractures treated with IMN were associated with decreased opioid requirements in the first 24 h after surgery. No effect was noted beyond 24 h after surgery. Extreme vigilance is essential in patients with tibia fractures to monitor for ACS, especially when PNB is utilized.

articles.title: From static fracture classification to dynamic clinical phenotypes: Feature-based longitudinal annotation and retrieval of comparable cases.
articles.abstract: Traditional surgical classifications provide standardized languages for describing clinical conditions at diagnosis, but they necessarily simplify complex and varying biological and mechanical phenomena into predefined categories. In fracture surgery, the AO/OTA classification has substantially improved communication and comparability by providing a standardized morphological framework. However, patients with apparently similar morphology at diagnosis may follow substantially different clinical trajectories after treatment. We propose a complementary approach based on feature-based annotations and longitudinal documentation of the complete treatment course. Rather than representing a patient solely by a static classification at time zero, this approach describes a dynamic clinical phenotype, comprising patient characteristics, fracture features, intraoperative events, postoperative course and outcome. Such structured longitudinal data enable the identification of comparable real-world cases beyond conventional classification subgroups. Artificial intelligence may facilitate the integration and analysis of these multidimensional data and, importantly, help identify when apparently similar clinical trajectories begin to diverge. This framework can support surgical education and shared decision-making by providing easy access to comprehensively documented comparable cases.

articles.title: Gabapentinoid-opioid co-prescription after long bone fracture fixation is associated with increased 1-year nonunion.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Gabapentinoids are increasingly incorporated into multimodal analgesia after orthopaedic surgery, yet their impact on outcomes following fracture fixation remains unclear. This study evaluated the association between early postoperative gabapentinoid-opioid co-prescription and clinical outcomes after operative fixation of closed long bone fractures.

METHODS: Using TriNetX, we identified opioid-naïve and gabapentinoid-naïve adults undergoing intramedullary or plate-and-screw fixation of isolated closed diaphyseal tibia, humerus, or femur fractures. Patients prescribed gabapentin or pregabalin and opioids within three days after surgery were compared with patients receiving opioids alone. Propensity score matching (1:1) incorporated demographics, medical comorbidities, fracture location, fixation method, mental health disorders, and substance use disorders. Primary outcomes were prolonged (30-90 days) and chronic (90-180 days) postoperative opioid use. Secondary outcomes included 30-day emergency department (ED) visits and readmissions, and 1-year nonunion and reoperation.

RESULTS: After matching, each cohort consisted of approximately 2000 patients (range, 1946-2012). Gabapentinoid-opioid therapy was associated with higher rates of prolonged (21.0% vs 16.1%; RR 1.31; p < 0.001) and chronic (9.8% vs 7.4%; RR 1.33; p = 0.007) postoperative opioid use. Gabapentinoid-opioid therapy was associated with fewer 30-day ED visits (25.1% vs 42.5%; RR 0.59; p < 0.001), while 30-day readmission rates were similar between cohorts (p = 0.174). One-year rates of nonunion (4.3% vs 1.9%; RR 2.21; p < 0.001) and reoperation (7.1% vs 4.2%; RR 1.68; p < 0.001) were significantly higher among patients receiving gabapentinoid-opioid therapy. In a sensitivity analysis that defined the opioid-only cohort based on the absence of gabapentinoid prescriptions during the first 3 postoperative days, rather than the 1-year postoperative medication window used in the primary analysis, the associations with prolonged and chronic opioid use and reoperation were no longer statistically significant, whereas the association with nonunion remained significant (RR 1.62; p = 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Gabapentinoid-opioid therapy was associated with fewer ED visits and higher rates of prolonged and chronic opioid use, nonunion, and reoperation; in sensitivity analysis, ED visits and nonunion remained significant, whereas opioid use and reoperation did not. These findings suggest that potential short-term analgesic benefits may be offset by adverse long-term outcomes, warranting caution and further study of gabapentinoid-opioid prescribing for acute perioperative fracture pain.

groups.journal: European Journal of Trauma & Emergency Surgery

articles.title: Fixation of patellar fractures using bioabsorbable hydroxyapatite/poly-L-lactide cannulated screws and subperiosteal nonabsorbable sutures.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Bioabsorbable implants offer a promising alternative to metallic fixation for patellar fractures, potentially avoiding hardware-related complications. In 2023, a new generation of bioabsorbable hydroxyapatite/poly-L-lactide (HA/PLLA) cannulated screws was introduced, featuring a low-profile (2 mm) trident-shaped head and increased root diameter for enhanced strength. This study evaluates the clinical outcomes of a surgical technique combining these redesigned screws with subperiosteal nonabsorbable sutures.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Between April 2023 and May 2025, 19 consecutive patients with transverse patellar fractures (AO/OTA 34-C1/C2) underwent open reduction and internal fixation. Two bioabsorbable cannulated screws were used. High-strength nonabsorbable sutures were passed through the screw channels and a central bone tunnel using a double-loop sliding knot for compression. The sutures were systematically routed subperiosteally to minimize tissue irritation. Full weight-bearing with a brace began on postoperative day one. Clinical and radiographic outcomes were assessed. This study was approved by the institutional review board of Kainan Hospital.

RESULTS: The mean maximum articular surface gap was 8.7 ± 5.2 mm. The mean follow-up was 8.6 ± 3.0 months. Bone union was achieved in all cases. At the final follow-up, the mean knee flexion was 138.7° ± 13.0° and extension was - 1.6° ± 3.4°. No postoperative complications, including infection, loss of reduction, screw breakage, or symptomatic hardware irritation, were observed during the follow-up period. No reoperations were required during the follow-up period.

CONCLUSIONS: All patients achieved bone union. No major complications or reoperations were observed during the follow-up period. These preliminary findings suggest that this technique may be feasible for transverse patellar fractures.

articles.title: Impact of pre-existing bleeding disorders on outcomes in patients with traumatic brain injury.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) remains a major global public health problem. This study aimed to evaluate the association between pre-existing bleeding disorders and clinical outcomes among patients with TBI. We hypothesized that pre-existing bleeding disorders would be associated with worse outcomes following TBI.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the 2021-2023 National Inpatient Sample (NIS) to evaluate the association between pre-existing bleeding disorders and clinical outcomes among patients aged 15 years or older hospitalized with TBI.

RESULTS: Mortality was significantly higher in the bleeding disorder group (13.9% vs. 4.8%; p < 0.001), the median length of stay was longer (5 days vs. 3 days; p < 0.001), median hospitalization costs were substantially higher (US $20,582 vs. US $13,515; p < 0.001), and discharge home was less frequent (44.8% vs. 61.6%; p < 0.001). After adjustment for age, comorbidity burden, injury severity, and other clinically relevant covariates, pre-existing bleeding disorders remained independently associated with higher odds of in-hospital mortality (adjusted OR, 2.31; 95% CI, 1.99-2.69).

CONCLUSION: Pre-existing bleeding disorders were independently associated with higher odds of in-hospital mortality after TBI. Patients with these disorders also experienced worse clinical outcomes. Early recognition and appropriate hemostatic assessment may support individualized management in this vulnerable population.

articles.title: 24-hour risk updating for major ICU complications after severe trauma: a prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Conventional trauma prognostic models rely primarily on admission data and cannot account for subsequent physiological response to treatment. We evaluated whether routinely collected physiological information available at 24 h provides incremental prognostic information for major intensive care unit (ICU) complications in severely injured patients.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective cohort of adults with severe trauma (Injury Severity Score [ISS] ≥ 15) admitted to the ICU between January 2024 and April 2025. The primary outcome was a composite of major respiratory, hemodynamic, renal, or septic complications during the ICU course. TRISS was compared with an admission ridge model incorporating ISS, Glasgow Coma Scale, hemoglobin, lactate, and international normalized ratio, and a 24-h updated ridge model additionally incorporating 24-h lactate and change in creatinine. Performance was internally validated with 1,000 bootstrap resamples.

RESULTS: Among 109 patients, median ISS was 29 (IQR 20-38), and 73 (67.0%) developed major ICU complications. Optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.788 for TRISS, 0.873 for the admission model, and 0.887 for the 24-h updated model; Brier scores were 0.178, 0.140, and 0.131. Compared with the admission model, the 24-h updated model improved performance (ΔAUC 0.016, 95% bootstrap interval 0.004-0.030; ΔBrier - 0.010, - 0.017 to - 0.005). Twenty-four-hour lactate and creatinine change were the strongest contributors to the update.

CONCLUSION: In severely injured ICU patients, incorporating physiological evolution during the first 24 h refined admission-based prognostic assessment. Lactate and creatinine trajectories provided incremental information for major ICU complications during the ICU course. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Addition of a McLaughlin cerclage to locking plate fixation of distal patellar pole fractures reduces interfragmentary displacement - a biomechanical human cadaveric study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate whether the addition of a McLaughlin cerclage to locking plate fixation of distal patellar pole fractures provides improved biomechanical construct stability and reduced interfragmentary displacement.

METHODS: A distal patellar pole fracture was simulated in sixteen fresh-frozen human cadaveric knees by a horizontal osteotomy in the distal third of the patella. Subsequently, locking plate fixation was performed. In a randomized half of the specimens, an additional McLaughlin wire cerclage was applied. The specimens were then subjected to 3000 cycles of extension starting at 90° of flexion under a maximum tensile load of 320 N. Using a Digital Image Correlation (DIC) system, the interfragmentary displacement between the proximal and distal fragments was measured at 1, 10, 20, 30, 50, 100, 500, 1000, 2000, and 3000 cycles. Statistical analysis was performed using repeated-measures ANOVA and Welch's unpaired t-t test at 3000 cycles.

RESULTS: An additional McLaughlin cerclage significantly reduced interfragmentary displacement under cyclic loading in comparison to locking plate fixation alone. After 3000 cycles, displacement was 2.27 ± 1.84 mm with plate fixation alone and 0.36 ± 0.22 mm with additional McLaughlin cerclage (mean difference 1.91 mm; 95% CI 0.38-3.45 mm; p = 0.0215).

CONCLUSION: An additional McLaughlin cerclage reduced interfragmentary displacement in distal patellar pole fractures. In cases of unstable distal pole patella fractures, the additional use of a McLaughlin cerclage may therefore be considered to enhance construct stability.

articles.title: Trauma care performance and patient outcomes - insights from a major trauma centre in Sweden.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Trauma is a leading cause of death among individuals under 45 years of age. Evaluating trauma system performance over time is important but inherently difficult due to concurrent changes in patient demographics, case-mix and care processes. The aim of this study was to describe temporal changes in patient demographics, injury severity and trauma care at a major trauma centre in Sweden from 2017 to 2023. We hypothesised that risk-adjusted 30-day mortality decreased and that time to computed tomography was reduced over the study period.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using data from the Karolinska Trauma Registry, including all trauma patients aged > 15 years fulfilling criteria for full trauma team activation, admitted between January 2017 and August 2023. Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess changes in 30-day mortality over time, adjusted for age, sex, injury severity category, ASA score and injury type. Time from arrival to computed tomography was analysed by linear regression and, because the distribution was skewed, by quantile (median) regression.

RESULTS: A total of 5,615 trauma patients were included. Over the study period, the patient population became older, and ASA scores increased, while injury severity and the proportion of penetrating injury remained unchanged. In multivariable logistic regression with 2017 as reference, the odds of 30-day mortality in 2022-2023 were lower (OR 0.61, 95% CI 0.43-0.88, P = 0.008) after adjusting for confounders. Median time to computed tomography decreased from 31 to 21 min; the adjusted difference in 2022-2023 compared with 2017 was - 7.5 min by linear regression (P = 0.014) and - 10.4 min by quantile regression (95% CI - 11.5 to - 9.2, P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Our findings are consistent with improvements in trauma care within a mature trauma system, with shorter median time to computed tomography and lower 30-day mortality despite an aging population with increasing comorbidity. However, the specific drivers of these changes are difficult to identify, and future studies should explore how individual components of pre-hospital and in-hospital care contribute to trauma outcomes.

articles.title: Chest tube fixation strength depends on suture caliber and fixation technique rather than tube diameter: a biomechanical cadaver study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chest tube dislodgement remains a relevant complication in emergency, trauma, and intensive care medicine. In a previous biomechanical study, the Modified Johannesburg technique using Mersilene USP 1 demonstrated superior fixation strength compared with other chest tube fixation techniques. The present study aimed to determine whether suture size, suture material, and chest tube diameter influence fixation strength.

METHODS: A prospective interventional biomechanical cadaveric study was performed using fresh porcine thoracic wall specimens. A total of 320 load-to-failure tests were conducted under standardized laboratory conditions. Two fixation techniques, Modified Johannesburg and Purse String, were compared using two chest tube diameters (20/28 Ch) and four non-absorbable braided suture configurations: Mersilene USP 1, Mersilene USP 2 - 0, Silk USP 1, and Silk USP 2 - 0. Each experimental group consisted of 20 specimens. Specimens were tested in a uniaxial testing machine until construct failure. Force [N] and elongation [mm] at failure were measured. The experiments were videotaped, and the failure mechanism was analyzed.

RESULTS: The Modified Johannesburg technique demonstrated significantly higher pull-out forces compared to the Purse String technique (125.0 vs. 66.4 N; p < 0.001), as did larger suture sizes (USP 1 vs. 2 - 0; p < 0.001) and Mersilene compared to Silk (114.6 vs. 76.9 N; p < 0.001). Chest tube size had only a very small and inconsistent effect on pull-out strength. The predominant failure mode was suture rupture (94.7%).

CONCLUSIONS: Chest tube fixation strength is significantly influenced by fixation technique, suture size, and suture material. The effect of chest tube diameter on fixation strength appeared negligible. The Modified Johannesburg technique, size 1 sutures, and Mersilene material provided superior biomechanical stability. Since failure occurred predominantly by suture rupture, the suture appears to represent the weakest link of the fixation construct.

articles.title: Changes in patellar height following suprapatellar and infrapatellar tibial nailing: a retrospective comparative cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Patella baja has been described after infrapatellar tibial nailing and may contribute to postoperative knee morbidity; however, whether the nail insertion approach influences postoperative patellar height remains unclear. This study compared longitudinal changes in patellar height (PH) after suprapatellar and infrapatellar intramedullary nailing for tibial shaft fractures. We hypothesized that the suprapatellar approach would better preserve patellar height.

METHODS: A retrospective comparative cohort study included 114 tibial shaft fractures treated with intramedullary nailing between 2016 and 2023, using a suprapatellar (n = 86) or infrapatellar (n = 28) approach. Patellar height was assessed using the Caton-Deschamps Index (CDI) on preoperative and final follow-up radiographs. The primary outcome was the longitudinal change in CDI (ΔCDI). Fracture union, complications, and reoperations were secondary outcomes.

RESULTS: The mean reduction in CDI was greater following infrapatellar than suprapatellar nailing (ΔCDI - 0.116 ± 0.173 vs. -0.011 ± 0.107; p = 0.001). After adjustment for baseline CDI and follow-up duration, this association remained significant (adjusted β=-0.055; 95% CI - 0.107 to - 0.004; p = 0.035), although sensitivity analyses showed attenuation after additional adjustment for sex. Fracture union rates were similar between approaches (93.0% vs. 92.9%; p = 0.987), with no statistically significant differences in complications or reoperations.

CONCLUSION: Infrapatellar tibial nailing was associated with a significant postoperative reduction in PH compared with the suprapatellar approach. This association persisted after adjustment for baseline CDI and follow-up duration but was sensitive to additional adjustment for sex. These findings highlight a potential relationship between nail insertion approach and postoperative PH but do not establish an independent effect of surgical approach.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Retrospective cohort study (Level III).

articles.title: Intraarticular calcaneal fractures: biomechanical analysis of two fixation constructs.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The aim of this biomechanical study was to investigate the fixation stability of a small low-profile 2.7 mm variable-angle locking anterolateral calcaneal plate supplemented with two additional independent cortex screws versus a traditional small 3.5 mm locking calcaneal plate in a standardized Sanders IIc fracture model.

METHODS: Sixteen fracture models cocomposed of three polymer blocks (fragments) each and simulating Sanders IIc intra‑articular calcaneal fractures were assigned to two groups. Group 1 (control) received a small 3.5 mm locking calcaneal plate, while Group 2 received a small 2.7 mm variable‑angle locking anterolateral calcaneal plate with two additional independent cortex screws. All constructs were instrumented using prefabricated pilot holes and standardized screw configurations. Biomechanical testing was conducted implementing a 3‑point-bending setup and progressively increasing cyclic loading to failure. Angular interfragmentary movements were quantified via motion tracking along with cycles to clinically relevant failure.

RESULTS: Initial stiffness (N/mm) in Group 1 (65.2 ± 34.7) was significantly lower versus Group 2 (232.5 ± 48.6), p = 0.020. Although angular interfragmentary movements around the anteroposterior axis were significantly greater in Group 1 versus Group 2 (p < 0.001), Group 1 demonstrated significantly smaller angular interfragmentary movements around the mediolateral axis for the central-to-posterior and anterior-to-posterior fragment pairs (p ≤ 0.004), while no significant difference between the groups was identified with regard to the central-to-anterior fragment pair (p ≥ 0.377). Cycles and loads (N) to clinically relevant failure in Group 1 (3635 ± 176 and 92.7 ± 3.5) were significantly lower versus Group 2 (17433 ± 628 and 368.7 ± 12.6), p < 0.001. Failure mode in Group 1 involved plate deformation, whereas Group 2 failed through breakage or bending of the independent cortex screws.

CONCLUSIONS: Biomechanically, fixation implementing a small low-profile 2.7 mm variable-angle locking anterolateral calcaneal plate supplemented with two additional independent cortex screws demonstrated stability comparable to, and in certain respects superior to that achieved with a small 3.5 mm locking calcaneal plate in a standardized Sanders IIc fracture model. However, the findings of this laboratory study do not establish an isolated benefit of the 2.7 mm plate itself, nor do they demonstrate clinical superiority or support alterations to postoperative weight-bearing protocols.

articles.title: Correction: Time to surgery and its impact on length of stay and mortality for neck of femur fractures at a major trauma centre.

Clinical outcomes of combined MPFL-reconstruction with MPTL-augmenting patellar distalization using hamstring autograft versus isolated MPFL in adolescents with patella alta: a retrospective comparative study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patella alta is a major risk factor for recurrent patellar dislocation in adolescents. This study aimed to compare the clinical outcomes of isolated medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) reconstruction with those of MPFL reconstruction augmented by medial patellotibial ligament (MPTL)-distalization, both using a semitendinosus hamstring autograft, in adolescent patients with patella alta.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted on 28 adolescent patients (mean age 11.2 ± 1.6 years; 9 males, 19 females) treated for recurrent patellar dislocation between May 2020 and July 2025. All patients had patella alta (Caton-Deschamps index > 1.2) and a history of at least one dislocation, with varying degrees of trochlear dysplasia (Dejour types A-B). All patients underwent MPFL reconstruction using a semitendinosus hamstring autograft harvested with preservation of its native distal tibial insertion, fixed via a single oblique transpatellar tunnel and femoral interference-screw fixation proximal to the distal femoral physis. Group A (n=14) underwent isolated MPFL reconstruction. Group B (n=14) underwent the same MPFL reconstruction with an additional MPTL-augmenting patellar distalization step using the same graft, secured by trans-osseous periosteal suture at the lateral patella. Surgical techniques emphasized physeal spare during reconstruction. Preoperative and postoperative assessments included the Kujala score, Lysholm score, Caton-Deschamps index, and sulcus angle. Follow-up averaged 12- 24 months. CT was performed using a low-dose pediatric protocol specifically for TT-TG measurement and trochlear bony morphology; MRI was used for soft-tissue and cartilage assessment. Group assignment was not randomized; patients with more pronounced patella alta and higher-grade clinical instability were preferentially treated with the combined procedure.

RESULTS: Both groups showed significant improvements in functional scores. In Group (A), Kujala scores improved from 59.3 ± 8.3 to 84.3 ± 5.1, and Lysholm scores from 50.3 ± 7.5 to 74.7 ± 9.3. Caton-Deschamps index decreased from 1.27 to 1.20. In Group (B), Kujala scores improved from 56.2 ± 7.4 to 88.9 ± 4.5, and Lysholm scores from 51.4 ± 7.6 to 87.4 ± 6.2. Caton-Deschamps index decreased from 1.28 to 1.11, indicating better patellar height correction. Complications occurred in 36% of Group A and 21% of Group B. Recurrent instability occurred in 2 patients (14%) in Group A and 1 patient (7%) in Group B; all were subluxation episodes managed non-operatively, and no revision surgery was required.

CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrated that MPFL reconstruction with MPTL-augmenting patellar distalization using a hamstring autograft yields greater functional improvements, superior patella alta correction, and fewer complications compared to isolated MPFL reconstruction in adolescents with recurrent patellar instability.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Retrospective comparative study; level IV.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical trial number: not applicable. This study is a retrospective comparative cohort study and does not meet the definition of a clinical trial as per the International Committee of Medical Journal Editors (ICMJE) guidelines, as it involves retrospective analysis of routinely collected clinical data without prospective intervention or randomization.

articles.title: Health economic evaluation of polytrauma treatment in the current aG-DRG system - Results of a Level I Trauma Center.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Resource-intensive polytrauma care is associated with high treatment and readiness costs and poses a financial challenge for hospitals. The aim of this retrospective single-center study of the years 2020 to 2022 was to analyze polytrauma reimbursements and costs.

METHODS: Based on billing and clinical data of 201 polytrauma cases from a German University Hospital and Level I Trauma Center, revenues and costs of the eleven MDC 21 A polytrauma DRGs were analyzed. Ratios of the revenue in relation to LOS, ventilation hours, OR time and implant costs as well as personnel costs were calculated. Contribution margins were determined as an upper-bound estimate.

RESULTS: DRG reimbursement was highest for the most severely injured patients (50,852 €, DRG W36Z). It was lowest for patients who died within five days (2,214 €, DRG W60Z) or without surgeries (4,056 €, DRG W61B). The contribution margin was also highest for the most severely injured patients (52,775 €, DRG W36Z). Revenues in relation to ICU LOS (3,455 €/day, DRG W36Z) and ventilation time (238 €/hour, DRG W01B) were lowest for the most severe polytraumas. Regarding OR time and implant costs, reimbursement was lowest for injuries of the spine, pelvis and extremities with 62 €/min (DRG W02B) and 5 €/€ (DRG W02A).

CONCLUSION: Treatment of polytrauma patients with long ICU stay, extended mechanical ventilation and multiple injuries of the extremities, pelvis and spine is not adequately reflected by the current per-case reimbursement in relation to the resources used (ICU days, ventilation hours, OR time and implant costs).

articles.title: Patterns, and outcomes of airbag -related penetrating injuries: a retrospective analysis from a level 1 trauma center.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The deployment of defective airbag inflators can generate high-velocity metallic fragments that cause face, neck or chest penetrating injuries with potentially lethal consequences. This study aimed to describe the injury patterns, management, and outcomes of suspected airbag-related penetrating injuries (ARPI) among patients in a Middle Eastern country.

METHODS: A retrospective observational study of patients presenting with penetrating injuries suspected of being related to defective airbag deployment. Data were obtained from the Qatar National Trauma Registry (QNTR), electronic medical records, emergency medical services (EMS), emergency department (ED), and Mortuary. Data were collected and analyzed descriptively.

RESULTS: A total of 16 patients had suspected ARPIs between April 2019 and February 2026. The mean age was 33.1 ± 8.3 years, and 93.8% were male. Metallic foreign bodies (FBs) from airbag inflator fragmentation were documented in 11/16 (68.8%) patients by imaging, and surgical removal while in 4/16 patients there were only entry-exit wounds after deployment of airbags following car crash. In one case, airbag deployed while mechanic was repairing a car steering wheel. Penetrating neck (43.8%), thoracic (31.3%), and maxillofacial injuries (31.3%), predominantly mandibular fractures, were most common. Surgical intervention was required in 11 (68.8%) patients and 7/16 required intensive care unit admissions. Five patients died (31.3%), including one at the scene (transported directly by the EMS, no CPR, and moved to the hospital mortuary), two died at the ED after unsuccessful CPR and two died during the hospital course (one presented with cardiac arrest and died on the sixth day and the other one required prolonged ECMO for acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and died after 4 months).

CONCLUSIONS: Airbag inflator rupture can produce serious injury patterns resembling patterns of ballistic trauma, characterized by penetrating neck wounds, maxillofacial fractures and thoracic injuries. These injuries are potentially associated with high mortality, surgical intervention, and critical care utilization. The full extent of these injuries is undetermined as some victims may have simply died at the scene without the benefit of trauma center evaluation or post-mortem examination.

articles.title: Guideline adherence in helicopter versus ground emergency medical services: an indication-based analysis of 129,783 patients from the TraumaRegister DGU®.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Helicopter emergency medical services (HEMS) are associated with higher intervention rates and improved access to specialized trauma centers compared with ground emergency medical services (GEMS). However, it remains unclear whether these differences reflect increased intervention intensity alone or more consistent implementation of guideline-recommended care. This study aimed to compare rates of selected guideline-recommended prehospital trauma interventions between HEMS and GEMS using a nationwide trauma registry.

METHODS: This retrospective multicenter cohort study was based on data from the TraumaRegister DGU® (TR-DGU) from 2016 to 2024. Adult patients (≥ 16 years) with severe trauma, defined as maximum Abbreviated Injury Scale (MAIS) ≥ 3, receiving physician-staffed prehospital care and primary admission to German trauma centers were included. After exclusion of secondary transfers, missing key data, and treatment in local trauma centers (level 3), 129,783 patients remained, of whom 25.0% were transported by HEMS. Rates of selected interventions recommended by the German S3 guideline on the treatment of polytrauma/severe injuries were assessed using predefined indication-based subgroups derived from available registry variables as surrogates for potential clinical indications to improve comparability between transport modalities. Analyses were performed descriptively.

RESULTS: Patients transported by HEMS were younger and more severely injured than those transported by GEMS (mean ISS 23.5 vs. 20.8; ISS ≥ 16: 72.9% vs. 65.4%) and more frequently presented with impaired consciousness and shock. Across all predefined indication-based subgroups, HEMS was associated with higher rates of the evaluated interventions, including advanced airway management in patients with impaired consciousness (96.5% vs. 82.9%), overall chest tube placement in patients with thoracic injuries consistent with pneumothorax (50.5% vs. 40.9%), with substantially higher rates of prehospital chest tube placement in HEMS (14.0% vs. 5.5%), pelvic stabilization in patients with pelvic injuries of AIS severity 3-5 (56.7% vs. 44.0%), cervical spine immobilization in cervical spine injuries (84.1% vs. 77.7%), and tranexamic acid administration in suspected major bleeding (48.7% vs. 22.8%).

CONCLUSION: In this nationwide trauma registry analysis, HEMS was consistently associated with higher rates of selected guideline-related interventions across predefined indication-based subgroups. By focusing on patients with predefined guideline-related indications, the present study aimed to improve comparability between HEMS and GEMS beyond crude intervention frequencies. Nevertheless, the observed differences should be interpreted in the context of the observational study design and residual indication-related confounding. Higher intervention rates do not necessarily indicate superior guideline adherence or quality of care in individual patients.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: III, retrospective comparative cohort study.

articles.title: Preoperative prevalence and risk factors for thromboembolic events following tibial plateau fractures: a retrospective analysis of an underestimated risk.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tibial plateau fractures (TPF) are complex intra-articular injuries carrying a high risk of deep vein thrombosis (DVT), muscular vein thrombosis (MVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE). Preoperative thrombosis is frequently clinically silent yet may cause serious complications, whereas its detection delays definitive surgery. This study assessed the prevalence and risk factors of preoperative venous thromboembolic events (VTE) in surgically treated TPF before and after implementation of routine duplex ultrasound screening.

METHODS: In this retrospective single-centre study at a level 1 trauma centre, all adult patients surgically treated for traumatic TPF (AO 41B/C) between January 2015 and August 2025 were reviewed (547 patients, 554 fractures). Until August 2020 duplex ultrasound (DUS) was performed only on clinical suspicion; from August 2020 onward routine preoperative DUS was progressively implemented. VTE were confirmed by DUS or CT angiography. Prevalences are reported per fracture and patient characteristics per patient; regression analyses were performed at fracture level, except for the patient-related model.

RESULTS: With DUS restricted to clinical suspicion (cohort A; 246 fractures), the detected prevalence of preoperative VTE was 3.7% (95% CI 1.9-6.8) and that of DVT 2.4% (1.1-5.2). Under routine screening (cohort B; 205 screened fractures) it was 20.0% (15.1-26.0) and 17.1% (12.5-22.8), respectively, 82.9% of DVT being distal. Given the different diagnostic strategies, this reflects the higher diagnostic yield of screening rather than a true increase in VTE. In cohort B, 28 of 41 VTE (68.3%) and 24 of 35 DVT (68.6%) were clinically silent. Two patients had in-hospital cardiac arrest from PE: one died from a DVT undetected before screening was introduced, the other had an asymptomatic DVT identified by screening. VTE was independently associated with pre-existing therapeutic anticoagulation (adjusted OR 2.96, 95% CI 1.10-7.98) and with the duration of external fixation (adjusted OR 1.11 per day, 1.02-1.20). High-grade closed soft-tissue injury (adjusted OR 2.41, 1.07-5.45), polytrauma (adjusted OR 2.24, 1.07-4.68) and initial external fixation (univariable OR 3.60, 1.76-7.35) were also associated with VTE, but none remained significant after accounting for fixation duration (adjusted OR 1.42, 0.52-3.89; 1.96, 0.76-5.05; 0.62, 0.12-3.27), i.e. risk was driven by time in the fixator rather than by external fixation as such.

CONCLUSIONS: Surgically treated TPF carry a substantial burden of preoperative VTE, and routine DUS reveals a high proportion of clinically silent thrombosis that would otherwise remain undetected. Severe closed soft-tissue injury, pre-existing therapeutic anticoagulation and, above all, the duration of external fixation may help to identify patients at increased risk. As two diagnostic rather than two treatment strategies were compared, the study cannot determine whether screening improves outcomes or reduces PE; prospective evaluation of structured screening and risk-adapted thromboprophylaxis is warranted.

articles.title: Emergency surgery for blunt abdominal trauma in polytrauma - the impact of time to laparotomy on outcomes.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Blunt abdominal trauma (BAT) is common in polytrauma patients. Emergency surgery is required for haemodynamically significant solid organ injury and intra-abdominal hollow organ injury. The effect of time to surgery on outcomes in patients requiring emergency laparotomy remains uncertain.

MATERIALS & METHODS: Adult polytrauma patients (ISS > 16) who underwent emergency laparotomy for blunt abdominal trauma between 1996 and 2020 from a trauma registry of a single level one trauma centre were included. Patients were divided into two groups based on the time elapsed from admission to emergency laparotomy: "Super Early" (≤ 60 min) and "Early" (60-180 min). Length of stay (LOS), intensive care unit (ICU)-LOS, ventilation time, re-look operations and mortality were assessed. Adjusted logistic regression was used to determine the independent predictive parameters, including timing of surgery, for mortality.

RESULTS: The study included 190 polytrauma patients with concomitant blunt abdominal trauma (mean age 42 years (± 17), median ISS of 36 (IQR: 19)). There were 95 patients in each group. Patients in the "Super Early" group had a compromised haemodynamic status and a higher ISS. Liver injury and serous membrane injury were more common in the super early group. The mortality rate was significantly higher in the "Super Early" group (51.6%) compared to the "Early" group (26.3%) (p < 0.001). Death due to haemorrhagic shock was significantly more frequent in the "Super Early" group (36.8%) compared to the "Early" group (13.7%) (p < 0.001). A regression model was adjusted to determine the independent predictors of mortality. Time to emergency laparotomy was not an independent predictor of mortality. However, increased ISS (OR = 1.04, p = 0.049), age (OR = 1.03, p = 0.037) and decreased systolic blood pressure (OR = 0.98, p = 0.025) were found to be significant predictors of mortality.

CONCLUSION: The timing of surgery showed no independent association with mortality as long as an emergency laparotomy was performed within 3 h of admission. The data suggests that patient-specific characteristics, injury severity and clinical status are more important for survival than the timing of an early emergency laparotomy. Future research should focus on determining the role of delayed laparotomy on outcomes in specific subgroups of patients.

articles.title: High-velocity trauma by social media: a new mechanism of injury in pediatric traumatology?
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Over the past two decades, social media challenges have emerged as a significant cause of injuries among adolescents. This study evaluates a sudden cluster of severe upper limb injuries resulting from the viral "Superman challenge" to raise clinical awareness of digital behaviors in pediatric trauma.

METHODS: A retrospective study at a tertiary pediatric trauma center evaluated patients aged < 18 years admitted in December 2024 following the "Superman challenge."

RESULTS: Eight patients were admitted within a 10-day window following high-energy injuries from the challenge. The cohort showed a female predominance (62.5%) with a mean age of 13.25 (±1.03) years. The high-velocity mechanism led to atypical, severe injury patterns distinct from routine accidental falls. We observed an unusual cluster of severe distal forearm fractures in five patients, which uniformly required surgical treatment. Three patients even suffered bilateral distal radius fractures. Additional associated injuries included fractures of the ulnar styloid process (n = 5) and concomitant TFCC tears (n = 2), reflecting the high-energy nature of the challenge.

CONCLUSIONS: The rapid, viral spread of physical social media challenges such as the 'Superman Challenge' can lead to dangerous injury mechanisms involving high-velocity trauma among children and adolescents. These trends could lead to sudden, localized clusters of atypical high-energy injuries-a scenario that, under specific conditions, risks overtaxing conventional healthcare systems, as previously demonstrated in the literature. Medical staff need to be aware of changing digital behaviors, which represent a new mechanism of injury in pediatric trauma.

articles.title: Surgical stabilization of rib fractures in a high-altitude trauma cohort: in-hospital clinical outcomes and resource use in a propensity score-weighted retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Surgical stabilization of rib fractures (SSRF) is increasingly used in the management of traumatic rib fractures, but its in-hospital outcomes in high-altitude trauma settings remain uncertain. We evaluated the association of SSRF with in-hospital pulmonary complications and length of stay in a high-altitude (≈ 3,500 m) trauma system.

METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of adults with CT-confirmed traumatic rib fractures admitted from 2015 to 2023 and managed with SSRF or non-operative management. Confounding was addressed using stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) with augmented outcome models; overlap weighting, propensity score matching, and time-dependent exposure analysis were used as sensitivity analyses. The primary outcome was a composite of in-hospital pneumonia, atelectasis, or respiratory failure. Pulmonary risk ratios (RRs) were estimated using modified Poisson regression, while ICU and hospital length of stay were analyzed using log-transformed weighted models.

RESULTS: Among 324 patients, 121 underwent SSRF and 203 received non-operative management. Before adjustment, SSRF patients had greater injury severity. In IPTW-augmented analyses, the pulmonary estimate was imprecise (RR 0.86, 95% CI 0.23-3.21; P = 0.822), and no significant difference was detected in ICU length of stay (exp[β] 1.04, 95% CI 0.97-1.10; P = 0.286). Hospital length of stay was longer with SSRF (exp[β] 2.31, 95% CI 2.02-2.65; P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Adjusted analyses found no statistically detectable difference in pulmonary complications or ICU length of stay, although the pulmonary estimate remained imprecise and does not establish equivalence or safety. SSRF was associated with longer hospital length of stay.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable.

articles.title: Pelvic hemorrhage in the context of demographic change: frequency and CT-based characterization of pelvic bleeding.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Traumatic pelvic hemorrhage is a major driver of morbidity and mortality in pelvic fractures. Classic literature described pelvic hemorrhage as predominantly venous, whereas arterial injury is considered less common. We evaluated the frequency, anatomical distribution, and presumed sources of pelvic hemorrhage in a contemporary trauma cohort using contrast-enhanced CT (CECT).

METHODS: We conducted a single-center, retrospective cohort study of consecutive patients with pelvic fractures treated at a level-I trauma center between 2020 and 2022. All patients underwent CECT at initial presentation. Two experienced pelvic trauma surgeons independently reviewed all scans. Radiologically relevant hemorrhage was defined by contrast extravasation, soft-tissue asymmetry/displacement, or a contained intrapelvic hematoma. Patients with and without hemorrhage were compared regarding age, sex, trauma mechanism, anticoagulation, and fracture type. The presumed bleeding sources were categorized as arterial, venous, cancellous, or mixed.

RESULTS: Radiologically relevant hemorrhage occurred in 95/512 (18.6%) patients and was more frequent after high-energy trauma and in men. Iliac sites predominated, whereas presacral bleeding was uncommon. The presumed bleeding source was cancellous in 44.2%, mixed in 29.5%, arterial in 18.9%, and isolated venous in 7.4%. Overall mortality was 7.0% and was significantly higher in patients with hemorrhage (14.7% vs. 5.3%; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: In this contemporary CECT-based cohort, pelvic hemorrhage was less frequent than historically reported, with CT findings most commonly suggesting cancellous or mixed bleeding sources. These findings suggest that the traditional concept of predominantly venous pelvic hemorrhage may not fully reflect current CT-based observations.

articles.title: The new trochanteric nail TFN-A has a higher complication rate in the treatment of proximal femoral fractures than the predecessor model PFN-A.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Trochanteric fractures (TF) are among the most frequent fractures and have major impact on the affected patients and the healthcare system. Cephalomedullary nails (CMN) are widely used for these fractures. Complications remain frequent, either due to comorbidities or concerning the implant. The goal of this retrospective, single-centre study was to compare the complication rates of two CMN from one manufacturer.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: All internal fixations TF performed between 01/2017 and 07/2021 in our institution were analysed retrospectively. Follow-up was at least two years. The CMN were the PFN-A or the TFN-A. Demographic data, all reoperations and revisions were recorded. Reoperations and revisions were estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method, with subgrouping as minor reoperation, minor revision or major revision, including conversion to total hip arthroplasty.

RESULTS: A total of 492 CMN, used in 475 patients, could be included. Among these, 248 were PFN-A and 244 were TFN-A. The overall reoperation rate was 15%, 12.9% for the PFN-A and 17.2% for the TFN-A, respectively. The TFN-A group had significantly more major revisions (hazard ratio 3.57 (95% confidence interval 1.42-9.94; p = 0.004).
